Declare the market inputs a value rests on

Source: R/market.R
pollin_market.Rd

The production and price that pollin_value() multiplies a ratio estimand by. quantity is current production, the output of the crop as it is pollinated now (for example area times yield), in unit; price is the price per unit in currency, in the prices of year. The value is ratio x price x quantity.

Usage

pollin_market(
  quantity,
  price,
  unit,
  currency,
  year,
  source,
  quantity_draws = NULL,
  price_draws = NULL,
  crop = NULL
)

Arguments

quantity

Current production, one positive number in unit.

price

Price per unit, one positive number in currency.

unit

Unit of quantity, one string (for example "t").

currency

Currency of price, one string (for example "AUD").

year

Price year, one whole number.

source

Where the inputs come from, free text printed with every value.

quantity_draws, price_draws

Optional numeric vectors of positive draws of quantity and price.

crop

Optional name of the crop, one string. It enters the attribution of each value, which pollin_guard_doublecount() reads; a value without a crop is taken to be of the same crop as any other.

Value

An object of class pollin_market: a list holding quantity, price, unit, currency, year, source, quantity_draws and price_draws (NULL when not given), and crop.

Details

Each input is a scalar, and may also be given as draws: a vector of positive values expressing its uncertainty. When draws are given they are used in place of the scalar, paired by index with the draws of the estimand, so their number must equal the number of estimand draws. The scalar is then the point value reported beside them. The package propagates the draws given; it does not model or forecast prices.

See also

pollin_value().

Examples

pollin_market(
  quantity = 12000,
  price = 650,
  unit = "t",
  currency = "AUD",
  year = 2024,
  source = "Illustrative inputs",
  crop = "canola"
)
#> <pollin_market>
#>   crop     : canola 
#>   quantity : 12,000 t 
#>   price    : 650 AUD per t 
#>   year     : 2024 
#>   source   : Illustrative inputs 

# Price uncertainty as draws
set.seed(1)
pollin_market(
  12000,
  650,
  "t",
  "AUD",
  2024,
  "Illustrative inputs",
  price_draws = rlnorm(4000, log(650), 0.1)
)
#> <pollin_market>
#>   quantity : 12,000 t 
#>   price    : 650 AUD per t (4000 draws) 
#>   year     : 2024 
#>   source   : Illustrative inputs
